title: Entering a new order
summary: Choose the patient and capture the ordering source’s request before acceptance and receipt.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: New order begins with the Patient step: Who is the order for? Type part of the name, the birth date or an identifier in the one search box, which has the focus when the page opens; the matching patients are listed as you type. Click a row, or move to it with the arrow keys and press Enter, to go on to Order details. Patients you entered orders for recently are offered under the box for one click. If nobody matches, Register patient sits right under the results, and you come back to New order with the new patient chosen. The exact searches by identifier or by name and birth date stay available under Exact search, which shows their fields directly and lists patients only after you search. Once a patient is chosen, the patient box (the identity banner) stays visible above the order form, with a Change patient link at its right end.

Order details follow the paper requisition in two steps. Step 1 of 2, Requisition, holds the top of the form (Ordering source: who sent it and who pays) and the bottom (Authority to test); Next: Tests checks the step and moves on. Step 2 of 2, Tests, holds the tests and panels with their sequence role and reflex testing, then the details only some requisitions have, behind small buttons with their counts. Back: Requisition keeps everything entered. The trail at the top shows Patient › Order details › Receive specimens › Finish receipt as rounded pills: a finished step is green with a check, the current step is filled blue with white text and a dot, and later steps are outlined. The choices with a few options (Received as, Billing responsibility, Template use, As supplied, Sequence role, Reflex testing) are rows of buttons where the chosen one is filled blue; a ? beside a label explains the field. Under each section title, one line says which part of the requisition it covers, and the section you last clicked or focused, anywhere inside it, keeps a blue border until you click or move into another one. On a typical desktop window the whole of step 1 fits without scrolling: Client, Client location and Ordering practitioner on one row, Received as, Billing responsibility and Template use on the next, and As supplied beside Document reference. Next to Next: Tests, a tip recalls that Enter or Next checks the step. The Order summary on the right ticks off Patient, Ordering source, Authority to test and Tests. Save order opens the saved order, which waits for an explicit acceptance on its page. Accept order and receive specimens saves the order, accepts it and goes on, on this page, to Receive specimens: the trail shows Receive specimens as the current step and the page is the same as Receive specimens (see that help), with its summary line, its three boxes and Next and Order beside them. Receive specimens creates the accession and opens Finish receiving; Cancel opens the accepted order, to receive later from its page.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Confirm the selected patient against the supplied identifying information before entering the request. Use Change patient if you selected the wrong record.

Enter requested tests, source order identifiers, diagnoses, medication details and evidence only as supplied. Missing information needs clarification through your laboratory’s process; it should not be invented to complete a form. Review the saved order to make sure it represents the request.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: If no clients or practitioners are available, a configuration administrator must register them. If no tests can be ordered, the catalog needs approved tests. Read field errors and correct the supplied entry; a failed save leaves the entered values available for correction.

sections.title: Corrected collection outside standing validity
paragraphs: An accepted order keeps its original standing-authority basis and reserved use. If corrected collection evidence is outside that authority’s validity period, testing and release remain blocked even after a quality review or later addition of a requisition. Correct an inaccurate date only from source evidence, or cancel the affected work when appropriate. The LIS does not silently replace the accepted order’s standing basis or release its reserved use.

pages.title: New order
pages.purpose: Choose the correct patient and record the ordering source’s exact request and evidence.
pages.access: Order-entry authority is required. Reads and decisions are recorded in the audit trail. The application checks your current permission and record state when you submit.

fields.name: Who is the order for? (find patient)
fields.meaning: One search box for the patient of the new order.
fields.values: The start of a family name, given names or full name (Given Family, Family Given or Family, Given), an exact birth date as YYYY-MM-DD, or the start of an active identifier value such as MRN-00001; up to 402 characters. Names ignore case and accents written differently; identifiers are case-sensitive; a partial birth date matches nothing.
fields.rules: Has the focus when the page opens. The list updates after a short pause in typing, or at once on Enter; Escape or the clear button empties the box. Former names are searched too, while rows show current demographics. The search text stays on this page: it is not put in the address or the audit trail, only that a search was used and how many patients were returned.

fields.name: Recent
fields.meaning: The patients you entered orders for most recently, one click away.
fields.values: Up to 10 patients, newest order first, each shown as name and birth date (YYYY-MM-DD).
fields.rules: Only orders you entered yourself count; a patient appears once however many orders they have. Hidden when you have entered no orders. Selecting one goes to Order details for that patient, so confirm the identity banner before continuing.

fields.name: Matching patients: Name / Birth date / Sex / Identifiers / Last order
fields.meaning: What tells the patients found apart before choosing one.
fields.values: Name as Family, Given with an identity-hold badge when a hold is open; birth date with the month as text and the age; administrative sex as supplied or Not recorded; active identifiers with their authority and type, or None recorded; the day of the patient's latest order (by anyone) and its client, or No orders.
fields.rules: Read-only. Shown once something is typed, with a count such as 3 patients match “test”. At most 25 patients are listed, then the count starts with First: type more to narrow the list. Compare at least two supplied identifiers; a similar name is not a match. The whole row is the choice: it highlights on hover and ends with ›.

fields.name: Exact search: Find by identifier / Find by name
fields.meaning: The exact patient searches, folded under Exact search.
fields.values: Find by identifier: Identifier, Assigning authority and Identifier type, compared exactly. Find by name: a family-name prefix, or the complete family name with a given-name prefix, and an optional real birth date in YYYY-MM-DD format (typed or picked from the calendar, which offers no day after today).
fields.rules: Closed when the page opens. Opening it shows the two forms and no patients; patients are read only after you run a search (Find by identifier or Find by name). The result rows show Name, Birth date, Administrative sex, Identifiers and Identity, 25 patients per page with Previous and Next, and a count above them. Choosing a row there also goes to Order details.

fields.name: Selected patient / Change patient
fields.meaning: The person for whom the request is being recorded.
fields.values: Read-only patient box (identity banner) after choosing a patient, with the Change patient link at its right end.
fields.rules: Confirm identity before entry. Changing patient leaves the current form; heed any unsaved-change confirmation.

fields.name: Client
fields.meaning: The configured ordering organization.
fields.values: Configured client name or code searched in the picker.
fields.rules: Required; no initial selection: the empty field reads Select…. Changing client clears Client location. Client, Client location and Ordering practitioner sit side by side on wide windows.

fields.name: Client location
fields.meaning: The ordering client’s location to which results are directed when supplied.
fields.values: Locations configured for the selected client.
fields.rules: Optional; disabled until a client is chosen, with the hint Choose the client first.; afterwards the hint reads Where results go, if the requisition names one. A location belonging to another client is rejected.

fields.name: Ordering practitioner
fields.meaning: The practitioner who ordered the tests.
fields.values: Configured practitioner identified by name/NPI.
fields.rules: Required; no initial selection: the empty field reads Select…. Missing practitioners need configuration before the order can be saved.

fields.name: Received as
fields.meaning: How the laboratory received the request.
fields.values: Paper requisition; Fax.
fields.rules: Required; not an electronic order interface. Shown as a row of buttons; select one, or use the arrow keys to move between them. Nothing is chosen at first.

fields.name: Billing responsibility
fields.meaning: Payment arrangement as supplied on the request.
fields.values: Third party (insurance); Patient (self-pay); Client (ordering clinic); Not supplied.
fields.rules: Required explicit choice. This initial fact does not substitute for confirming the detailed order billing selection. Shown as a row of buttons; select one, or use the arrow keys to move between them. Nothing is chosen at first. The ? beside the label explains it.

fields.name: Template use
fields.meaning: Whether a clinic template supplied the requested tests.
fields.values: No template; Clinic template.
fields.rules: Required. On the same row as Received as and Billing responsibility; Clinic template adds Template name under Received as and Confirmed for this patient (compact Yes and No buttons) under Billing responsibility. Selecting a template never selects tests automatically. Shown as a row of buttons; select one, or use the arrow keys to move between them. Nothing is chosen at first. The ? beside the label explains it.

fields.name: Template name
fields.meaning: Name of the clinic template actually used.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters.
fields.rules: Required only for Clinic template.

fields.name: Confirmed for this patient
fields.meaning: Whether the practitioner confirmed the template’s tests for this person.
fields.values: Yes; No.
fields.rules: Required when Clinic template is selected. Record the source answer; do not assume confirmation. Shown as Yes and No buttons.

fields.name: Clinic order number / Issued by
fields.meaning: Identifier assigned by the clinic and the clinic or system that numbered it.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters each.
fields.rules: Both supplied together or both blank. Expand the folded Clinic order number and source references (marked Optional) to enter them.

fields.name: Source document reference
fields.meaning: Reference to the source requisition.
fields.values: Text, up to 1000 characters.
fields.rules: Optional; it is a reference, not a document-upload control.

fields.name: Facility setting
fields.meaning: Setting supplied with the order.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters.
fields.rules: Optional; no suggested setting.

fields.name: Tests ordered
fields.meaning: Approved configured tests and panels actually requested by the source.
fields.values: Current approved catalog choices identified by code, name, test or panel kind and required specimen types.
fields.rules: Choose at least one; none is preselected. Find each test or panel with the search at the top of Tests; each version can appear once. Chosen tests are listed below the search, one row each with its sequence role, reflex testing and × to remove it. Removing a test also removes its unsaved sequence and reflex choices.

fields.name: Find tests / Find reflex tests for …
fields.meaning: Finds the tests and panels to order, and the reflex tests of a long catalog.
fields.values: Part of a configured code, name or required specimen-type code; Test or Panel also matches the displayed kind.
fields.rules: Find tests is always the search at the top of Tests, reading Search tests and panels by name, code or specimen type while no test is chosen. Find reflex tests is shown when more than 15 choices are available; shorter reflex scopes are checkboxes. Type to narrow the popup, then choose an option or use Arrow Down and Enter. The popup stays open and the search clears after a choice so you can pick several; Escape closes the popup. In Find tests each chosen test shows inside the field as a chip with its code and name and its own ×; × on a chip removes that test, and Backspace in an empty search removes the last one; either also removes its row below. Free text is not an ordered test. Searching does not remove chosen tests. Scroll the popup or narrow the search to reach other choices. Ctrl+A (Command+A on macOS) selects the search text for replacement. Enter in the search does not save the form.

fields.name: Show — tests or reflex scope
fields.meaning: Limits the long catalog to configured tests, panels or both. Each reflex scope has its own filter.
fields.values: Tests and panels; Tests only; Panels only. Initially Tests and panels.
fields.rules: Shown beside the search for more than 15 choices. This is a browsing preference, not a requested test. Changing it preserves all chosen tests and their entered details.

fields.name: Chosen tests
fields.meaning: The complete unsaved selection, including choices that are outside the current search or Show filter.
fields.values: A chip in the search field and one row below per chosen test: its name in bold and its code on the left, then Sequence role, Reflex testing and × on the same line (stacked on a narrow window). Before any choice: No tests chosen yet. Search above for each test or panel marked on the requisition. Reflex scopes show a selected count, and long ones a separate Chosen reflex tests list.
fields.rules: Review this list against the requisition. Complete sequence role and reflex permission for each ordered item; choosing a panel does not independently select or substitute its component tests.

fields.name: Sequence role
fields.meaning: The test’s explicit place in the requested sequence.
fields.values: First-line (screen); Confirmation.
fields.rules: Required for every selected test; initially blank. Shown as a row of buttons in the test's row, beside its Reflex testing; screen readers hear it as Sequence role for the test. The ? beside the label explains it. Never inferred from a method’s certainty or a panel name.

fields.name: Reflex testing
fields.meaning: Whether the source permits reflex work from this test.
fields.values: Authorized; Not authorized; Not stated.
fields.rules: Required for each selected test; initially blank. Shown as a row of buttons in the test's row; screen readers hear it as Reflex testing for the test. Authorized reveals that test’s reflex scope. The × at the end of the row removes the test.

fields.name: Reflex tests authorized
fields.meaning: The explicitly permitted scope of reflex testing.
fields.values: Other currently approved configured tests or panels; short lists use checkboxes and long lists use Find reflex tests for … with the Show filter.
fields.rules: Shown only when reflex testing is Authorized. When the catalog has no other approved test or panel, it reads No other tests or panels in the catalog to authorize as reflex tests, and the authorization saves without a scope. Choose only the supplied permitted scope. Selected scope stays visible when searched or filtered and can be removed individually. This records permission; it does not order or perform those reflex tests immediately.

fields.name: Authority to test: As supplied
fields.meaning: The evidence of the source’s authority or intent to order, from the bottom of the requisition.
fields.values: Handwritten signature; Electronic signature; Documented intent to order; Not supplied.
fields.rules: Required explicit choice on step 1, Requisition. Missing authority can lead to a clarification hold at acceptance. Shown as a row of buttons; select one, or use the arrow keys to move between them. Nothing is chosen at first. The ? beside the label explains it.

fields.name: Authority to test: Document reference
fields.meaning: Where the authority evidence can be located, such as the signed requisition's number.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters. The empty field reads Such as the signed requisition's number.
fields.rules: Optional, beside As supplied. Do not claim a signature that was not supplied.

fields.name: Order details · step 1 of 2 / step 2 of 2
fields.meaning: Which part of the requisition is being entered: Requisition, then Tests.
fields.values: Read-only. The current step is highlighted in the step bar below the patient box. On step 2, Requisition shows a green check and green text, and the line on to Tests turns thicker and green.
fields.rules: A task position, not a clinical status. Moving between steps never discards entries.

fields.name: Order summary: Patient / Ordering source / Authority to test / Tests
fields.meaning: What the order still needs before Save order works.
fields.values: Each part shows a green check circle when done, or an empty circle while still to do; screen readers hear Done or To do before the part. Patient is done once the patient is chosen; Ordering source when Client, Ordering practitioner, Received as, Billing responsibility and Template use (with Template name and Confirmed for this patient for a clinic template) are chosen; Authority to test when As supplied is chosen; Tests when at least one test is chosen and each has its sequence role and reflex testing.
fields.rules: Read-only. The line below reads Save order works once the required fields are filled in, or All required fields are filled in. The engine checks every entry again when the order is saved.

fields.name: Only if the requisition has them: Diagnoses (n) / Medications (n) / Point-of-care results (n) / Standing authority
fields.meaning: Supplied details that many requisitions do not carry, shown as small buttons with the number entered.
fields.values: Each button opens its part below: the diagnosis, medication or point-of-care rows with their Add buttons, or the Patient-specific standing order picker.
fields.rules: Optional and closed when step 2 opens. A part with entries, or a chosen standing order, stays open so its fields and any error on them stay visible.

fields.name: Order billing (empty)
fields.meaning: The order's billing selection, which is added on the saved order.
fields.values: A warning, Order billing is empty, while it is not being added; a note, Order billing opens after saving, once Order billing or Add order billing is selected.
fields.rules: A warning, not a block: you can save without it, and billing for this order is held until it is added. Billing responsibility on step 1 records what the requisition says; it does not replace the order billing selection.

fields.name: Diagnoses: Code / Code system / Code system version / Source document
fields.meaning: Each diagnosis exactly as supplied, together with its coding context and provenance.
fields.values: Code and system text, optional system version, source reference; up to 1000 characters per text field.
fields.rules: Diagnosis rows are optional. In each added row, Code, Code system and Source document are required; system version is optional.

fields.name: Pre-printed on the laboratory's form
fields.meaning: Whether the diagnosis was already printed on the laboratory form.
fields.values: Yes; No.
fields.rules: Required in each added diagnosis row. It distinguishes supplied evidence from a patient-specific diagnosis decision.

fields.name: Medication as written / Code / Code system
fields.meaning: The supplied medication statement and optional coded representation.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters for each field.
fields.rules: Medication rows are optional. Medication as written is required; code and code system must be supplied together or both blank.

fields.name: Medications: Reported by / Reporter's name
fields.meaning: Source category and named reporter for the medication statement.
fields.values: Reported by: Ordering clinic; Patient; Other. Reporter’s name: source text up to 1000 characters.
fields.rules: Source category required per row; name optional.

fields.name: Provided on / List current as of
fields.meaning: When the medication information was supplied and the date it describes.
fields.values: Dates entered as YYYY-MM-DD. Type it, or pick it from the calendar button in the field.
fields.rules: Optional. A missing as-of date remains unknown; the list is not assumed current.

fields.name: Point-of-care results: Device or test / Drug / Result as written / Reported by
fields.meaning: Attributed external point-of-care observations supplied with the request.
fields.values: Source text, up to 1000 characters per field.
fields.rules: Rows are optional; each of these fields is required in an added row. Result text is preserved as written and never becomes a laboratory result.

fields.name: Performed at, as written
fields.meaning: Collection or performance timing stated for an external point-of-care result.
fields.values: Free source text, up to 1000 characters.
fields.rules: Optional; retain uncertainty rather than invent a timestamp.

fields.name: Patient-specific standing order
fields.meaning: Optional supplied authority selected for the displayed patient and ordering practitioner.
fields.values: Blank by default; choices show source reference, inclusive collection dates and accepted uses/limit.
fields.rules: Changing practitioner clears the selection. Does not select tests or replace source evidence. Expired-at-intake authority may still apply to an earlier valid collection; unknown/outside dates block testing/release. Exhausted authority cannot accept a new use.

actions.name: Choose a patient (row or recent patient)
actions.does: Chooses the patient of the new order.
actions.availableWhen: A matching row or a recent patient is shown. Click the row or the recent patient, or move to a row with the arrow keys and press Enter.
actions.result: Order details opens for that patient, with the identity banner above the form and Patient ticked in the trail.

actions.name: Exact search
actions.does: Opens or closes the exact patient searches.
actions.result: Shows the Find by identifier and Find by name forms directly. After a search, the matching patients are listed with Previous and Next; choosing a row goes to Order details.

actions.name: Register patient
actions.does: Starts the two-step registration process from New order.
actions.availableWhen: On the Patient step, under the results (Not in the list?), and in Exact search when nothing is found. Order-entry authority is required.
actions.result: Enter source details and review matches before saving; New order then opens with the registered patient chosen.

actions.name: Change patient
actions.availableWhen: A patient is selected: the link at the right end of the patient box.
actions.result: Returns to Who is the order for?. Choose and verify the replacement patient before continuing; any unsaved-order warning must be addressed.

actions.name: Add diagnosis / Add medication / Add point-of-care result / Remove …
actions.does: Adds or removes an evidence row in the unsaved request.
actions.result: Only the submitted rows are saved; each added row must satisfy its required fields.

actions.name: Remove — chosen test or reflex scope
actions.does: Removes an ordered test and its own sequence/reflex fields, or removes one test from an authorized reflex scope.
actions.availableWhen: The corresponding test is selected; ordered tests have × (Remove) at the end of their row, and long reflex scopes have Remove beside each chosen scope item.
actions.result: Updates the unsaved request. Other selected tests and their details remain. Searching or changing Show alone never removes a choice. Focus returns to the selection control.

actions.name: Next: Tests
actions.does: Checks step 1, Requisition, and moves on to step 2, Tests. Enter in a field of step 1 does the same.
actions.availableWhen: On step 1, at the end of the form, after the tip Tip: Enter or Next checks this step and moves on to Tests.
actions.result: When a required choice is missing, step 1 stays open with each missing field marked; otherwise step 2 opens and its heading takes the focus.

actions.name: Back: Requisition
actions.availableWhen: On step 2, at the start of the action row, while the order is not being saved.
actions.result: Step 1 shows every value entered; the tests and details of step 2 are kept too.

actions.name: Apply the first test's choices to all tests
actions.does: Copies the first chosen test's sequence role and reflex testing to the other chosen tests.
actions.availableWhen: On step 2 with more than one test chosen.
actions.result: Each test keeps its own reflex scope; change any test afterwards as the requisition states it.

actions.name: Diagnoses / Medications / Point-of-care results / Standing authority (buttons)
actions.does: Opens or closes that optional part of step 2.
actions.availableWhen: On step 2. A part with entries stays open.
actions.result: Shows the part's rows and Add button, or the standing order picker.

actions.name: Order billing / Add order billing
actions.does: Marks the order to have its billing added right after saving.
actions.availableWhen: On step 2. Order billing is a toggle; Add order billing is in the empty-billing warning.
actions.result: After Save order or Accept order and receive specimens, the saved order opens with its Order billing section open, ready to confirm the billing selection; the order is not accepted here and Receive specimens does not open. Selecting Order billing again undoes this.

actions.name: Save order
actions.does: Records the request and supplied evidence.
actions.availableWhen: On step 2, with order-entry authority, once the Order summary shows every part done.
actions.result: Opens the saved order in Received, not yet accepted state. If the application refuses a field of step 1, step 1 opens with the field's error.

actions.name: Accept order and receive specimens
actions.does: Saves the request, then accepts it: pressing it is the explicit acceptance, recorded in the audit trail. The application rechecks authority, clarification holds and any standing order first.
actions.availableWhen: On step 2, once the Order summary shows every part done; accessioning authority in addition to order-entry authority.
actions.result: Order received and accepted, then Receive specimens, on this page. If the order cannot be accepted (for example a hold, missing authority, or a failed standing-order check that places a hold), Order received, not accepted is shown and the saved order opens on its page with the reason.

actions.name: Receive specimens
actions.does: After acceptance, records the tests for this material, the collection and the specimens received as a new accession.
actions.availableWhen: Once the order is accepted and nothing required is missing.
actions.result: Opens Finish receiving for the new accession, to print labels and record each receipt decision. A refused entry keeps every value for correction.

actions.name: Cancel (after acceptance)
actions.availableWhen: After acceptance, while nothing is saving.
actions.result: Opens the accepted order; Start receiving specimens there continues later. Typed input asks for confirmation first.

actions.name: Cancel
actions.does: Leaves order entry. In the Order summary on the right.
actions.availableWhen: While the form is not saving.
actions.result: Leaves order entry; the full-page unsaved-changes guard asks before discarding a changed order.

restrictions: All request choices begin blank; no tests, diagnoses or medical-necessity statements are prepopulated.
Order text is limited to 1000 characters per field and must not contain control characters. Clinical cutoffs and interpretations are not entered here.
Saving a request, accepting it and receiving specimens are separate decisions; Accept order and receive specimens makes the first two with one explicit press, and receiving stays its own step.
No standing-order creation or cancellation editor is provided by this form.

Practice templates do not independently authorize patient testing. Select only supplied standing authority and enter requested scope independently. Retired clients, locations and practitioners are excluded from new-order choices; historical orders retain them.
workflow: Find the patient by name, birth date or identifier, or pick a recent patient; register the patient when nobody matches. Then verify the identity banner.
Step 1, Requisition: choose the ordering source from the top of the requisition and the authority to test from the bottom, then select Next: Tests.

Step 2, Tests: add only the requested tests or panels with the search at the top (for a long catalog, Show also narrows it; you can type the next code immediately after choosing an item). Review Chosen tests against the source, set each test’s explicit sequence role and reflex permission, and choose any authorized reflex scope.

Open Diagnoses, Medications, Point-of-care results or Standing authority only when the requisition supplies them. Select Order billing to add the order's billing right after saving, or save without it.
Save order to leave the order for acceptance on its page, or Accept order and receive specimens to accept it and go on to Receive specimens.
After acceptance, on Receive specimens: keep or choose the tests, enter the collection as supplied and each specimen received, then Receive specimens and continue on Finish receiving.

troubleshooting.problem: A save fails or a field is rejected.
troubleshooting.recovery: Read the message and correct the indicated value. The open form retains entered values after failure; success is shown only after the application accepts the save. Cancel abandons an unsaved dialog.

troubleshooting.problem: No clients, practitioners or tests are available.
troubleshooting.recovery: Have configuration staff register the missing ordering source or approve the necessary catalog test. Do not substitute another client, practitioner or test.
Supply both the clinic’s number and its issuing authority, or leave both blank when absent.
Supply its code system as well, or leave both coding fields blank and retain the source text.

troubleshooting.problem: No matches in Find tests or a reflex search.
troubleshooting.recovery: Clear or shorten the search and set Show to Tests and panels. Search the configured code, name or specimen-type code; synonyms are not added automatically. Existing choices remain below the picker. If the exact requested item is still absent, obtain catalog clarification rather than substituting another test.
